Why go: a floating party for a big group

The Beat Boat is a 72 ft motor catamaran fitted out for events: a DJ booth, a 16-speaker sound system with four subwoofers, LED lighting, a bar, a dance floor, a shaded lounge and four toilets. It takes up to 70 guests, and an event manager on board runs the day, so the host can enjoy it too. Birthdays, hen and stag groups, company parties and weddings are its usual business.

Shorter charters run to Koh Som off Samui's north coast for a sunset session, or across to Koh Phangan's east or west coast. The full days add the Five Islands, Ang Thong or Koh Tao, with snorkelling and paddle boards between sets.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: groups of 20–70 who want music, drinks and a party atmosphere on the water.
  • Choose something else if you want peace and quiet: a sailing catamaran is calmer.
  • Smaller group? At under 15 people, a yacht charter costs much less per head.

Good to know

  • Drinking and swimming: most boat-party accidents happen when guests swim after drinking. The crew can stop swimming if they judge it unsafe.
  • Ang Thong: closed from 1 November to 15 December each year.
  • Costs: bar prices on board are resort-level; for big groups a pre-ordered drinks package or BYO with the fee is usually cheaper.
  • Weather: the boat is large and stable, but open-water routes are rough in the monsoon.

Planning an event

Book four to six weeks ahead for peak dates such as Christmas, New Year and Songkran. Agree the music, catering and drinks plan with the event manager in advance, and send a guest count a week before. For corporate groups, ask about a photographer and drone package so you don't need to bring your own.
